# Upālipañcaka (Pvr 17)
**ID:** Pvr 17
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Upālipañcaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-pvr17
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul13.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Upālipañcaka* is the seventeenth text of the *Parivāra* in modern editions, though designated as chapter fifteen in traditional arrangements and early Western editions, opening at Vin V 180 [von Hinüber 1996; Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 6; Norman 1983]. Set at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, the text is framed as an extended dialogue between the Buddha and Venerable Upāli, the foremost master of monastic discipline (*vinayadhara*) [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 6; SuttaCentral]. It comprises fourteen sub-chapters containing 149 questions regarding Vinaya rules, offenses, and legal proceedings, with the Buddha's responses systematically structured into sets of five factors or qualities [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 6; Norman 1983; Stache-Rosen 1984; SuttaCentral]. For example, it details five disqualifying criteria that bar a monk from being granted leave to make an accusation against another, such as impure bodily conduct, speech, or livelihood [Vinayamukha 1983]. Norman observes that this pentadic structure parallels the decimal groupings of the *Upālivagga* in the Aṅguttara Nikāya as well as the Parivāra's own *Ekuttarikanaya* [Norman 1983].
Scholars have highlighted the distinct textual status of the *Upālipañcaka* within the *Parivāra*. Manuscripts preserve a concluding colophon (*Parivāram niṭṭhitaṃ*) at the end of the preceding fourteenth chapter (*Kaṭhinabheda*), after which the *Upālipañcaka* begins abruptly like a Khandhaka text, suggesting that the original compilation may have concluded at that point and that the *Upālipañcaka* is a later addition [von Hinüber 1996; Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 6].
Close counterparts exist across Buddhist traditions. In the Tibetan canon, the twelfth treatise of the *Vinaya-uttara-grantha*—titled *Upāliparipṛcchā*—directly corresponds to the *Upālipañcaka* [Banerjee 1979]. A Chinese translation of an *Upāliparipṛcchā* (associated with the Abhayagirivāsin or Sarvāstivādin traditions) precisely parallels the opening section on the qualifications for independence at Vin V 180, though it contains only five questions rather than the 149 of the Pali text [Stache-Rosen 1984; Norman 1983]. A Sanskrit fragment from Central Asia, however, diverges from the Pali text [Norman 1983]. SuttaCentral identifies internal curated parallels in Pvr 7 (*Ekuttarikanaya*) and Pvr 14 (*Anuvijjakassapaṭipatti*) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects extensive text reuse with the *Kammakkhandhaka* (Kd 11), the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), and the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as alignments with Tibetan Vinaya treatises and Sanskrit Vinaya texts including the *Śayanāsanavastu* and *Adhikaraṇavastu* [DharmaNexus]. Complete English translations have been made by I. B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 6; SuttaCentral].
